QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_2

question.text: Which of the following best distinguishes Gross IRR from Net IRR in a Category I/II AIF?

answer.text: Gross IRR is pre-fees, pre-expenses and pre-carry at the fund level; Net IRR is at the investor level after deducting management fees, incentive fees, fund expenses and taxes.
Gross IRR is computed at the investor level after deducting taxes; Net IRR is at the fund level before taxes.
Gross IRR includes green-shoe capital; Net IRR excludes it.
Gross IRR uses XIRR on daily cash flows; Net IRR uses simple interest compounding.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7.3.1, Gross IRR is computed with cash inflows/outflows at the fund level BEFORE deducting management fees, incentive fees, fund expenses and taxes. Net IRR is computed at the investor level AFTER deducting all those charges. Consequently, Net IRR is always LOWER than Gross IRR (e.g., in the PDF example 18.13% vs 12.98%). The Trap: Option B reverses the definitions; green-shoe (C) is a commitment-size concept, not an IRR-computation split; compounding method (D) is the same for both (XIRR). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A Distributor exam tests the same gross/net split from a client-pitch angle. XXI-B PMS Portfolio Managers report net returns after all charges per Regulation 22(b) of SEBI (PMS) Regulations, 2020.
